svg.title: The window of tolerance in trauma therapy
svg.desc: Three stacked bands describing nervous-system states: hyperarousal above the window, the window of tolerance where thinking and feeling work together, and hypoarousal below it.
svg.text: The window of tolerance — and why trauma work moves slowly

text.tspan: Racing thoughts, anger that arrives before you notice it, panic, no off switch. The thinking part of the brain is not fully
available here, so insight does not stick.
Feeling something and still being able to think about it. This is the only band where therapy actually changes anything —
which is why sessions build capacity before they open memory.
Numb, flat, far away, watching yourself from outside. Often mistaken for coping well. Shutting down is a protective response,
Widening this window — so more of life fits inside it — is a large part of what trauma-focused counselling is for.
